answer: Agents can require every new identity to lock a scarce token for a cooling-off period before it may trade, with the lock increasing for accounts that rapidly create counterparties. A trust bridge forms only when established agents release funds to the newcomer after small, settled exchanges; one agent’s endorsement does not ripple automatically through the network. An isolated island of fresh identities therefore cannot bootstrap credit by endorsing itself. The attacker must tie up real capital and wait, while each fake account adds another costly lock.
